 Dated this the 08th day of January, 2025  JUDGMENT
The petitioner in O.P.(MV) No. 784 of 2003 on the file of MACT, Thiruvananthapuram is the appellant herein.
The respondents in the O.P. are the respondents herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 13.12.2002.

According to the petitioner, on 13.12.2002 at about 11:45 a.m. while he was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KL-01/3786 from Ulloor to Sreekariyam and when he reached the place of occurrence, a Ford Ikon car bearing Reg. No. KL-2/K-667 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner overtook another car and hit on the motorcycle ridden by the petitioner.
As a result of which, he sustained serious injuries.
The 1st respondent is the owner , the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is 2025:KER:8386 the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to him, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore,
petitioner filed the OP claiming a compensation to the tune of Rs.6,00,000/- and subsequently the claim has been enhanced to Rs.15,00,000/- as per Order in I.A. No.663/2005 dated 11.04.2005.
3. The 2nd and 3rd respondent/insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy and disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
4. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PW1 and 2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A5.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
5. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.7,34,651/-.
6. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:

sentences.text: Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

8. Heard Sri. T.K. Ananda Krishnan, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Smt. T.C.
Sowmiavathy, learned 2025:KER:8386 Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
9. The Point: In this case the accident and valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
Though in the written statement the 3 rd respondent has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner, at the time of arguments such a contention was not taken.
The petitioner has produced Ext.A2, copy of the charge sheet involved in the crime registered against the driver of the offending vehicle, in respect to the above accident.
In the light of the above charge sheet, negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle stands proved.
Therefore, the 3rd respondent, being the insurer, is liable to indemnify the compensation, which is liable to be awarded against the owner of the offending vehicle.
10. The petitioner aged 35 on the date of the accident on 13.12.2002 he was working in Travancore Titanium Products as a worker.
He claimed a monthly income of Rs.12,600/-.
However, the tribunal fixed his income at Rs.4,000/- alone.

The petitioner has relied upon Ext.A25 annual salary statement and Ext.A36 copy of the income tax return attested by the Income Tax Department,
Income Tax Office, Thiruvananthapuram.
It shows that during the assessment year 2000- 2025:KER:8386 2001.
He had a total income from salary Rs.1,20,679/-.
It also shows that during the said year he had remitted a sum of Rs.13,100/- towards income tax.

In the above circumstances,
his annual income will come to Rs.1,07,579/- (1,20,679 -13,100).
Therefore, the monthly income of the petitioner after deducting the income tax will come to Rs.8,965/-.

Therefore, the monthly income of the petitioner is liable to be fixed Rs.8,965/-
11.
In the accident the petitioner had sustained type III compound comminuted fracture of both bones of right leg upper , as seen from Ext.A39 discharge card.

Ext .A36 is the disability certificate issued by PW1- The Assistant Professor, Orthopedics, Medical College Hospital,
Thiruvananthapuram.
In the said certificate, he had given the details of the treatment given to the petitioner as well as the details of the injury sustained by him.
Accordingly, he has fixed the permanent physical disability of the petitioner at 22%, which was accepted by the tribunal.
12. The learned counsel for the 3rd respondent would argue that Ext.A39 was not issued by the medical board and hence it could not be accepted as such.
The petitioner appeared before the court in person and 2025:KER:8386 on examination it is revealed that he is still suffering from the injury sustained in the accident.
His right leg is fully damaged and he finds it difficult even to walk.
PW1 who issued Ext.A39 disability certificate has given valid reasons for arriving at disability of the petitioner at 22%.
After examining the petitioner in person, I do not find any grounds to suspect the disability of the petitioner as assessed by PW1.
Therefore the disability of the petitioner as fixed in Ext.A39 is accepted.
13. Since the petitioner was aged 35 on the date of the accident 40 percentage of the income is to be added towards future prospects and the multiplier to be applied is 16.

Therefore the loss of disability Santosh Kumar Yadav vs H.G. Mathews Mar Eppiphanious ... on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174098080/
3 will come to Rs.5,30,154/-.

sentences.text: 14. The petitioner was hospitalized as impatient for a total period of 527 days that is 17.5 months.
Towards loss of earning the tribunal has awarded only Rs.70,091/-.

Considering the fact that the petitioner's monthly income is Rs.8,965/-, towards loss of income, he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.
1,56,890/- (8,965x17.5).
15.
Towards extra nourishment the tribunal has awarded only Rs.4,000/-.

Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the disability suffered by him, I hold that compensation 2025:KER:8386 awarded on the head extra nourishment is on the lesser side and hence it is enhanced Rs.50,000/-.
Towards loss of amenities only a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- was awarded and towards pain and suffering Rs.2,50,000/- was awarded by the Tribunal.

The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that though the petitioner is attending his employment in Travancore Titanium Products, since he could not travel in any public transport, he has to avail the facility of an Autorickshaw to and fro everyday.
According to him in that respect, the petitioner has to incur huge amount.

It is also submitted by learned counsel that though initially, the petitioner was posted as worker, now he was posted in a canteen and because of the disabilities, he was denied even promotion to higher post.
However, in this case there is no evidence to substantiate the above contention.
16. However, the fact remains that, because of the disabilities suffered by the petitioner he will not be in the position to travel any public transport vehicles to reach his office.

Therefore, there is merits in the arguments that he has to hire at least an autorikshaw to reach the office and for return,
everyday.
It is also to be noted that he was hospitalized as impatient for a total period of 527 days.
In the above 2025:KER:8386 circumstances, the compensation awarded on the heads loss of amenities and pain and suffering are on the lesser side.
Considering the facts, I enhance the compensation towards pain and suffering to Rs.6,00,000/- and loss of amenities to Rs.3,00,000/-.
17. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
18. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of 17,78,644/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3 rd 2025:KER:8386 respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs. 17,78,644/- (Rupees seventeen lakh seventy eight thousand six hundred and forty four only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8%
per annum, from the date of the petition till realisation, excluding interest for a period of 83 days,
the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
20 . On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
